repositories.name: Tool-call guard benchmark
repositories.description: Which Decision Model guards an agent's tool calls

paragraphs: DefenseClaw guards an AI coding agent's tool calls in three tiers: deterministic rules, then a Decision Model (DefenseClaw calls this tier System One), then the Gemma 4 LLM judge on the cases the Decision Model is unsure of. This Space asks which Decision Model should sit in that tier, and whether adding it helps. Part of DefenseClaw, with Small language models as tool-call guards and Cisco Skill Scanner vs NVIDIA SkillSpector.

OpenJev weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). Evaluation-only: nothing here is approved for training, synthetic data generation, teacher context, distillation or redistribution, and source payloads are withheld.
features: What this is: the guard, its three tiers, the data and the shared false-block budget of 13 wrongly blocked calls out of 3,381 benign.

The answer: put OpenJev in the Decision Model tier. Block-only F1 0.712 to 0.752 (escalate-on-confirm; 0.738 as the cascade runs today), false blocks 23 to 14 of 3,381, judge traffic 100% to 16%. At 99% benign traffic,…
Which model: 12 candidate Decision Models at the shared budget. open-jev-qwen-27b (F1 0.739) and OpenJev (0.712) lead with overlapping intervals; the recommended stack is measured at 14 false blocks.
What it costs: 2 of 19 policies are undominated; per-call enforcement spares 2.7 to 5.1 times more benign work than per-session.
Does it fail safe: 24 of 28 injected Decision Model faults end with the call allowed.

repositories.description: Ultra-fast local NVFP4 video + synchronized audio generation

paragraphs: Joint video and synchronized sound from MiniMax-H3, rebuilt for a single 96 GB Blackwell ZeroGPU worker.

MiniMax-H3's published model card notes that about 13B parameters live in AdaLN-related branches and that their outputs can be precomputed for inference. The pruned checkpoint makes that concrete: it samples the shared timestep embedding curve at 1025 points and linearly interpolates an 8-value coordinate for each requested timestep. Every block's modulation projection consequently becomes [96768, 8] instead of [96768, 2688].

The four large matrices in each of the 50 blocks—fused QKV, attention output, MLP up/gate and MLP down—are NVFP4. The modulation curve, norms, embeddings, biases and final heads stay at higher precision.

paragraphs: GOTabPFN: From Feature Ordering to Compact Tokenization for Tabular Foundation Models on High-Dimensional Data

GOTabPFN is designed for high-dimensional tabular datasets where standard TabPFN-style predictors become difficult to use directly due to large feature counts. It takes a raw feature matrix and labels, learns an ordered and compressed representation, and then performs prediction using a frozen TabPFN-2.5 head.

GOTabPFN is not limited to biomedical datasets. It can be applied to any high-dimensional tabular dataset with a compatible feature matrix and target labels, including biomedical, transcriptomic, text, sensor, and image-feature datasets.
features: GO-LR learns a global feature order Pi from cluster-wise feature graphs.
NSC segments the ordered feature axis and compresses each segment into a compact meta-feature.
TabPFN-2.5 performs prediction on the compressed token vector Z(x).
